note: Rabban Gamliel, Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya, Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Akiva went up to Jerusalem after the Temple was destroyed. At Mount Scopus they tore their clothes, and on the Temple Mount they saw a fox come out of the place of the Holy of Holies. The others wept and Akiva laughed. They said: of this place it is written that an outsider who approaches shall die, and now foxes walk in it; shall we not weep? He answered that Scripture links Uriah's prophecy that Zion would be plowed like a field with Zechariah's that old men and women would again sit in Jerusalem's streets. Now that the first has come true, the second surely will. They said: Akiva, you have comforted us.
why: It follows an earlier journey of the same Sages, when Rabbi Akiva laughed at the noise of Rome while they wept. Both carry the discussion's theme of exile and hope for redemption, and this story closes the tractate.
